title: Transporting a counter-saving run
statement: Let $Q$ and $T$ be types with decidable equality, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $d$ be a four-tape configuration on the input obtained by embedding each bit of $x$ as a digit. Suppose $d$ is in the counter-decrement phase, its input-head position $p$ satisfies $p\le |x|$, and a Boolean word $w$ has binary value $2^{|w|}-1$ with $p$ strictly less than that value. Suppose tape 3 stores the digit-embedded word $w$, with the symbol at word index $i$ stored at tape coordinate $i$ minus the position of the tape-3 head. Then for some $t\le 5(p+1)+2|w|$, the embedded counter-saving machine reaches the escape state with input-head position zero and tape 3 storing the digit-embedded word obtained by applying the fixed-width decrement operation $p+1$ times to $w$; all other configuration components are unchanged. Before time $t$ it reaches neither the done state nor the escape state, and at every time through $t$ each work-tape head remains within distance $|w|+1$ of its initial position. The bitwise complements of the resulting counter word have binary value $p+1$.
